name: Question 4
worked_solution:
From the vector addition and scalar multiplication rules, we have

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}[2f(t)+3g(t)]\,\text{d}t=2{\int }_{0}^{2}f(t)\,\text{d}t+3{\int }_{0}^{2}g(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}[2f(t)+3g(t)]\,\text{d}t & =2{\int }_{0}^{2}f(t)\,\text{d}t+3{\int }_{0}^{2}g(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =2⟨{e}^{2}-1,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡2,\,3⟩+3⟨3,\,-1,\,5⟩ \\  & =⟨2{e}^{2}-2,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡2,\,6⟩+⟨9,\,-3,\,15⟩ \\  & =⟨2{e}^{2}+7,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡2-3,\,21⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Calculate ∫02[2f(t)+3g(t)]dt given that ∫02f(t)dt=⟨e2−1,sin⁡2,3⟩ and ∫02g(t)dt=⟨3,−1,5⟩.

a
⟨4e2+3,2sin⁡2+9,12⟩
b
⟨7e2,2sin⁡2−3,21⟩
c
⟨2e2,6sin⁡2,21⟩
d
⟨2e2−7,sin⁡2+3,9⟩
e
⟨2e2+7,2sin⁡2−3,21⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the vector addition and scalar multiplication rules, we have

∫02[2f(t)+3g(t)]dt=2∫02f(t)dt+3∫02g(t)dt.

Therefore, ∫02[2f(t)+3g(t)]dt=2∫02f(t)dt+3∫02g(t)dt=2⟨e2−1,sin⁡2,3⟩+3⟨3,−1,5⟩=⟨2e2−2,2sin⁡2,6⟩+⟨9,−3,15⟩=⟨2e2+7,2sin⁡2−3,21⟩.
